title: Numerical Imputation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of numerical imputation.
Apply or inspect a Scikit-learn API or workflow related to numerical imputation on a small example.
Identify a relevant assumption, validation need, or failure mode and document how to check it.

content.intro: This lesson covers Numerical Imputation in the Data Preprocessing and Feature Transformation module. It preserves the source syllabus topic and subtopics, then adds an original explanation, a runnable reference example, and a practice task.
content.why_it_matters: Preprocessing determines how raw values become model inputs. Fit learned transformations only on training data and reuse the fitted transformation unchanged at prediction time.

content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: The example learns a median from the training rows and uses it for the missing entry. In a real evaluation, fit the imputer only on training data. For numerical imputation, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
X = np.array([[1.0], [np.nan], [3.0]])
print(SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit_transform(X).ravel().tolist())

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Check input shapes, target alignment, data types, missing values, label order, and whether the expected output assumes a fixed random seed. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data, preferably inside a Pipeline. Do not select parameters by repeatedly looking at the final test set.
